items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: So, he gave me a job at the Americano with Ralph Font's orchestra

ctx.x: Well, I went to Puerto Rico -- I called a friend of mine from New York and asked him what the situation was down there and he said, 'Well, in the national band -- the state band, they'd like to have a bassoon player.' I said, 'Okay, I'm coming down.' So, we arrived in Puerto Rico on a

Sunday night and by Tuesday night I was working with the National Orchestra -- National Band, playing bassoon. They didn't have a decent bassoon player on the Island at that time. But the gimmick was, it only paid $200.00 a month. Mind you, $200.00 a month. But we had some aid. I stayed with my sister-in-law and her husband is one of the important horse trainers there and they had a big house, so they kept the four of us until I got on my feet. So I just turned over my -- when it got to me it was $190.00 a month…

oboe player they didn't have. So, whenever an act came there that they needed a piccolo or oboe or bassoon, why I would go to the various hotels. So I did that for another couple years or so. And I met a trumbone player who was a jazz man from L.A., but he was making his living down there selling encyclopedias. Got rich. And also was a good jazz man. He couldn't read music but he could play. Very big guy -- Bob Smiten. So he introduced me to another fellow who I found out later on was president of Williams…
